newsitem.title: USA: White House names key aides to Clinton.
newsitem.headline: White House names key aides to Clinton.

text.p: The White House named several key aides to President Bill Clinton on Wednesday, picking Rahm Emanuel as his senior advisor for policy and strategy and John Podesta and Sylvia Mathews as deputy chiefs of staff.

Incoming White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles also told reporters that the president had chosen James Steinberg, the chief of staff at the State Department, and Army Brig. General Donald Kerrick, as deputy national security advisers.
Emanuel, a long-time White House aide, will fill the shoes of George Stephanopoulos, one of Clinton's closest aides since his successful 1992 campaign for the presidency.
Podesta, now a visiting professor of law at Georgetown University, previously served as the White House staff secretary.
Mathews, currently chief of staff to Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, previously worked under Rubin on the White House National Economic Council.
White House Political Director Doug Sosnik will now serve as counsellor to the president, and Victoria Radd, a Washington lawyer, has been tapped to be Bowles' chief of staff.

In announcing the appointments, Bowles stressed that the new White House staff, which is expected to be in place by January 20, would work together as a team. Many White Houses have been marked by sharp infighting.
"I have set about to build a team ... a team with sharp minds but not sharp elbows," Bowles said.
Bowles said the White House hoped to announce several more Cabinet officers on Friday, but gave no details.
